property.name: hint
property.value: The old shaft has caved in. Cold air seeps between the stones.

property.name: text
property.value: The rubble bursts apart. Behind it, a shaft drops away into the dark.

property.name: weak_hint
property.value: The stones barely shift. It would take a blow that shakes the ground itself.

property.name: lines
property.value: They came at dawn for the tithe, same as every new moon. This time we were three sacks short. | Todd says you'll go after Grok. Gods keep you, stranger.

property.name: lines
property.value: The well's gone bitter since spring - since the goblins started digging up at the stone ring. Tastes like an old copper pot. | Mind the bridge. The stones get slick when the mill runs hard.

property.name: lines
property.value: Fish are floating belly-up downstream. Something up there is rotten. | Hush. Even sick fish can hear you.

property.name: speaker
property.value: Old Fisherman

property.name: lines
property.value: Goblins at the Harlan farm! West, past the bridge! | Please - the Harlans are still in there!

property.name: speaker
property.value: Frightened Woman

property.name: lines
property.value: Don't go west, they'll cut you down! ...Unless you mean to fight them?

property.name: speaker
property.value: Frightened Man

property.name: lines
property.value: No Gift in Millbrook, so no soldiers for Millbrook. Every new moon Grok's tax-men come for our grain instead. Short a sack, and a barn burns. | We can't pay you much. But end Grok, and Millbrook will owe you everything. | Take the north road past Brookside. Greystone land starts at the war totem.

property.name: lines
property.value: Your blade's seen honest work. Bring back Grok's tusk and I'll hang it over the village gate. | My grandfather swore an old swordsman out of the three kingdoms lived out his days in the copper mine. Never once drew his blade, they said. The deep shafts caved in long before my time.

property.name: lines
property.value: Three barns this year. Grok's tax-men want our grain for the winter. | If you go after Grok, mind the torchbearers. They set everything alight.

property.name: lines
property.value: Bread, rope, lamp oil. Half my flour goes up the Greystone road as Grok's tithe. | Heading north? Mind the meadow - the thornbacks spit spikes.

property.name: lines
property.value: ...cold. Always cold, since the water went green. | Grandmother says the green will make me strong. It only makes me tired.

property.name: speaker
property.value: Goblin Child

property.name: title
property.value: The Stone Ring

property.name: stage_name
property.value: Brookside Trail

property.name: hint_text
property.value: The falls run green at the edges. Whatever fouls the water is up on the high ground.

property.name: hint_text
property.value: A goblin war totem. Greystone land begins here.

property.name: stage_name
property.value: mine=The Hollow Caves;camp=Greystone Camp

property.name: hint_text
property.value: Hob's chest: a spare flask (+1) and an old mantra scroll. You learned EARTHSHATTER.

property.name: locked_text
property.value: The bear watches you from the dark. Nothing gets near that chest while it lives.

property.name: hint_text
property.value: A dying seer whispers: "The hooded one came in spring, swinging a red lantern and singing. He said if we dug up the stone ring, our sick young would heal. We dug. The water turned green. Grok drank his medicine... and became something else."\n\n"Before the green water, our grandmothers' grandmothers had names like yours."

property.name: hint_text
property.value: Fresh digging. The trench runs toward the ring - and the water in it smells green. The slabs heaved out of it bear a noble house's crest, worn almost smooth.

property.name: intro_line1
property.value: You let ONE swordsman chase you off a farm full of grain?!

property.name: intro_line2
property.value: Useless maggots! Get out of my sight!

property.name: wake_line
property.value: Get UP, you worms! Tear him apart!

property.name: intro_line3
property.value: And you... you smell of nothing. No Gift in you at all.

property.name: depart_text
property.value: The ground gives way - you fall into the dark beneath the ring!

property.name: hint_text
property.value: Nailed over the village notices, in crude red paint: "BY ORDER OF GROK, CHIEF OF GREYSTONE - MILLBROOK OWES TWENTY SACKS OF GRAIN EACH NEW MOON. SHORT SACKS, BURNT BARNS." | Beneath it, in a careful hand: "Grain store: seven sacks. Winter is three months off. - Todd"\n\nPasted over an older notice, under a red wax seal: "BY GRACE OF THE ETERNAL KING - every child of age who takes the Gift at the Chapel of the Vale is AWAKENED, and kept under the King's protection." No soldier has ever come to collect a child from Millbrook.

property.name: speaker
property.value: Notice board

property.name: hint_text
property.value: Boot prints in the mud, spilled grain, drops of pitch from a torch. The raiders fled north along the stream - toward Greystone land.

property.name: hint_text
property.value: Claw marks gouged into the stone, and a warm, rotten breath rising from below. Something breeds down there - and it is hungry.

property.name: hint_text
property.value: Grok's tusk - proof that Millbrook is free. Then the ring shudders. Something deep below turns over, like a sleeper in the dark - and the stones begin to sink...

property.name: say
property.value: What - the ground's giving way!

property.name: hint_text
property.value: A note nailed to the post: "The bear took the old copper mine - and my iron chest by the shaft. In it: a spare flask and the mantra scroll my father brought down from the old cloister on the ruins road. I can't read the thing. Whoever puts that brute down, keep them both. And leave the caved-in shaft be. My father worked the deep vein behind it until the day he heard something down there that clicked whenever he moved, and went quiet when he stood still. He brought the roof down on it himself. - Hob of Millbrook"

property.name: text
property.value: Short on the tithe? Then burn it all!

property.name: text
property.value: Help! The farm is burning!

property.name: text
property.value: Hah! Tell your headman - Grok wants his grain!

property.name: text
property.value: Raiders! They came down the north road!

property.name: text
property.value: You there, with the sword - please, help us!

property.name: after_hint
property.value: Grok's camp lies north - past Brookside Trail, beyond the war totem.

property.name: line1
property.value: Gods be thanked - you drove them off! I'm Todd, headman of Millbrook.

property.name: line2
property.value: Grok's goblins take our grain every new moon. We came up short - so they burned the Harlan farm.

property.name: line3
property.value: We're farmers, not fighters. End Grok and bring me his tusk - and Millbrook is free.

property.name: locked_text
property.value: Millbrook is still burning. I can't just walk away.

property.name: say
property.value: Not now... these people need help first.

property.name: say
property.value: That camp's crawling with hexers. Hob's mantra scroll first - the old mine is west.

property.name: hint_text
property.value: A cloister brother's copper flask, tucked behind the old wall. Every drink now heals more.

property.name: stage_name
property.value: ring=The Stone Ring;ruins=Cloister Ruins

property.name: script
property.value:
fade out 0.01
slide Story/prologue_1: For 1,176 years, one kingdom has stood where three once warred - and one king has ruled it for every one of those years.|He does not age. He does not die. His people call him the Eternal King.
slide Story/prologue_2: Every child knows how it began. A holy man, the Ascended, ended the age of war - and was murdered by Thrag, a jealous king.|His most faithful apostle, Darwin, cut the murderer down and bound the warring crowns into one realm. Heaven blessed him with a life without end.
slide Story/epic_gift_light: In the Year 780, a light rose from the holy ground where the Ascended once wept for His people - green as the fields that grew wherever He walked.|The King proclaimed it the Tears of the Ascended: His last gift, kept sealed since His death for the day His people would need it.
slide Story/epic_gift_strong: All who drank grew strong. The sick rose from their beds. One pair of hands could lift what four had carried, and men worked from dawn to dark without tiring.|Since that day, every child of age drinks the Tears at the Awakening.
slide Story/epic_classes: Above all stand the great Houses, blessed by Heaven at the King's side. They do not grow old.|Below them, the Awakened: soldiers and labourers, strong with the Gift and protected by the Crown.
slide Story/prologue_4: Last come the Unawakened - those who never drank. No soldier marches to save their villages.|And in the hills, the goblins: those who drank from wild springs instead of the King's cup. So the priests say.
slide Story/prologue_6: It is the Year 1176 of the Eternal King. Ren is a wandering swordsman. He has never taken the Gift.|He draws his blade for those no soldier will defend. It pays poorly. He keeps doing it.|This year the ground itself has begun to tremble across the Greystone Plains. No one can say why.
slide Story/prologue_7: On the morning of the new moon, smoke rises over the village of Millbrook. Ren quickens his pace.
slide end
fade in 1.2
